page.layout: One page of text, one column, no marginal notes. Running head at top with page number at top right. Main text runs down the page, with the heading "DE AVARITIA." mid-page and a final line at the foot.

main_text.p: χἰκμ̄ ἡ [?]πλεονεξίᾳ, eamq; tanto minus exple ri posse, quo plures prouinciæ & opes in potestatem illius venirent.

De seniore Dionysio memoriæ proditum est, eum, cum circa initium tyranni-dis, in regia, à Syracusanis συγομαχῆσαι [?] obsessus, in summo vitæ discrimine versaretur: & amici hortarentur, ut depofito imperio vitam redimeret: conspicientem bouem à lanione uno ictu prostratum, dixisse: Quum mors adeò breuis sit, an'nō absurdum fuerit, mortis metu tale regnū deponere?

Jam vero, si quidam vel mortis periculo regnum sibi esse redimendum existimant: quid animi Principibus ambitiosis & regnandi cupidis esse dicemus, qui magnos habent successus: & quorum conatibus vix quisquam dehortatione modesta ἀντοφθαλμῷ [?], nedum omni conatu resistere audet? Nihil dubium est, eos magis magisq; & plura habendi, & pluribus imperandi libidine exardescere. Crescit enim regnandi amor, cum accessione ignorum: ut σύμφυτον νόσημα [?].
main_text.head: DE AVARITIA.

page.notes: Greek words in the first line, in the paragraph "De seniore Dionysio" and in the last paragraph are uncertain at the letter level; marked [?]. The word "ignorum" in the last paragraph is probably a misprint for "ignorum" as printed; left as printed. Final line is partly cut at the foot; "&c." is read as printed. Scan shows no catchword or signature.
